correctness.rationale: For every n>=2, h>=2, 0<p<1, and uniform seed after deletion, the deterministic identity h*N_h-(h-1)*N_(h+1)=number of vertices in open components of size >=h yields an exact piecewise-affine expected count F_m. Its positive slope for m>=h and explicit positive difference (h-1)p^h between both-long and one-short splits prove every threshold-risk minimizer. Connected-pair probabilities give H_m with strictly increasing discrete increments, proving exactly the central mean minimizers. Their intersection occurs iff n<=2h, and at n>=2h+1 the risk gap is (h-1)p^h/(n-1). The standalone exact-rational checker reproduces 16,376 deterministic identities, 252 F_m cases, 36 mean-pair cases and 1,089 policy instances; finite tests are not substituted for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Risk-sensitive allocation asks to minimize an event of at least h cases rather than expected cases. The result provides an exact all-order and all-threshold classification of which vertex should be protected, a sharp generic incompatibility threshold n=2h+1 and a quantified risk penalty. The distributional run-count identity applies to a natural path contact topology and avoids relying on a single tiny numerical counterexample. The observation remains a mathematical benchmark, not a claim of empirical treatment efficacy; small absolute tails can have limited public-health relevance for very large populations.
